newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT DRAGGED DOWN BY NYMEX GASOLINE.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT DRAGGED DOWN BY NYMEX GASOLINE.

text.p: IPE Brent crude was dragged down on Monday on the back of weaker than expected NYMEX gasoline, but views were mixed on the overall short-term trend, brokers said.

"The market is still fundamentally weak and we are following Friday's downward trail. The real test will be in the evening when most traders expect the market to go to $18.10 (a barrel for September Brent)," one broker said.

The prompt Brent contract traded down four cents at $18.44 a barrel by 1450 GMT. NYMEX September gasoline, called to open steady to 0.25 cent a gallon higher, moved last down 0.44 cent at $61.55 cents a gallon.
Others saw September NYMEX WTI heading higher before the close. The contract was last done up six cents at $19.60.
"We see it heading up to $19.70 and leading us into a new level today," another broker said.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Rasheed said on Monday that Iraq planned to export 30 million barrels of crude by the end of August - equivalent to 1.5 million barrels per day.
"This isn't new. The market has been gearing up for this for a few weeks now and it would take more than that (volume) before the market would panic", another broker said.
August gas oil was last done down $1.25 at $168.25 a tonne but volume trade was light.
